name: Energy
scope: Oil, gas and related energy value chain (exploration, production, refining, transport, storage, marketing).

name: Materials
scope: Mining, metals, chemicals, construction materials, paper/forestry and other industrial inputs.

name: Industrials
scope: Manufacturing, machinery, aerospace/defense, transport, logistics and engineering services.

name: Consumer Discretionary
scope: Non-essential consumption: autos, retail, luxury, travel, leisure, hospitality, restaurants, e-commerce.

name: Consumer Staples
scope: Essential consumption: food, beverages, household and personal care products.

name: Healthcare
scope: Pharma, biotech, medical devices, providers, diagnostics and life sciences.

name: Financials
scope: Banks, insurers, asset managers, exchanges, brokerages and consumer finance.

name: Information Technology
scope: Software, semiconductors, hardware, IT services, cloud and cybersecurity.

name: Communication Services
scope: Telecom, wireless, internet platforms, social media, digital advertising, streaming and media.

name: Utilities
scope: Electricity, natural gas, water and regulated utility services.

name: Real Estate
scope: REITs and real estate owners/operators/developers across major property segments.

name: Growth Expectations
scope: Investor expectations regarding future economic activity over the next 6-24 months, capturing GDP trends, PMI signals and central bank outlooks.

name: Inflation Expectations
scope: Anticipated future price pressures and their impact on monetary policy, interest rates and asset valuations.

name: Monetary Policy & Liquidity
scope: The cost and availability of capital in the global financial system, encompassing central bank rate decisions, balance sheet policy and credit conditions.

name: Financial Conditions & Market Stress
scope: The ease with which households, businesses, governments and investors can access financing; includes credit spreads, volatility and systemic risk indicators.

name: China Macro
scope: China-specific growth, trade, manufacturing and commodity demand dynamics given the country's outsized role in global economic activity.

name: Structural & Geopolitical Regimes
scope: Long-term forces reshaping the global economic system, including trade fragmentation, energy transition, demographic shifts and geopolitical realignment.

name: Earnings, Profitability & Business Performance
scope: Company-level earnings, margins and revenue trends as the primary driver of long-run equity returns and valuations.

name: Investment, Capex & Innovation Cycles
scope: Corporate investment spending, capital expenditure plans and R&D activity as determinants of future productive capacity and growth.

name: Capital Structure, Financing & Capital Allocation
scope: How companies finance operations and distribute capital to investors through debt, equity issuance, buybacks and dividends.
